source_text:
Ἀπροσδεής, ἀδελφοί, ὁ δεσπότης ὑπάρχει τῶν ἁπάντων: οὐδὲν οὐδενὸς χρῄζει εἰ μὴ τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι αὐτῷ.
φησὶν γὰρ ὁ ἐκλεκτὸς Δαυείδ: Ἐξομολογήσομαι τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ ἀρέσει αὐτῷ ὑπὲρ μόσχον νέον κέρατα ἐκφέροντα καὶ ὁπλάς: ἰδέτωσαν πτωχοὶ καὶ εὐφρανθήτωσαν.
καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Θῦσον τῷ θεῷ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως καὶ ἀπόδος τῷ ὑψίστῳ τὰς εὐχάς σου: καὶ ἐπικάλεσαί με ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεώς σου, καὶ ἐξελοῦμαί σε, καὶ δοξάσεις με.
θυσία γὰρ τῷ θεῷ πνεῦμα συντετριμμένον.
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, urging them away from faction by showing that what God truly wants from people is not sacrifice but confession, praise, and a broken spirit.
pass_a_gloss: Without need, brothers, the master is of all things: nothing of anyone he needs except the to confess to him. For says the elect David: I will confess to the Lord, and it will please him more than a young calf horns bringing forth and hooves: let the poor see and let them rejoice. And again he says: Sacrifice to God a sacrifice of praise and give back to the Most High your vows: and call upon me in the day of your affliction, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me. For a sacrifice to God is a spirit broken.

choices.why: The adjective describes God as having no lack or requirement; 'without need' keeps the privative force of the alpha-prefix visible.
The term denotes absolute ownership and authority over all things; 'master' preserves the lord-servant relation without importing the covenant overtones of 'Lord'.
The verb means open acknowledgment or declaration, here directed to God; 'confess' captures the act of declaring God's praise and one's dependence.
The phrase is a direct echo of Psalm 50:19 LXX (Psalm 51:17 English); 'broken spirit' is the standard rendering and preserves the sacrificial metaphor.

bible_refs.note: Ἐξομολογήσομαι τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ ἀρέσει αὐτῷ ὑπὲρ μόσχον νέον κέρατα ἐκφέροντα καὶ ὁπλάς

pass_b_english: Brothers and sisters, the Master of all things lacks nothing. He needs nothing from anyone except one thing: that they confess to him.
For David, one of the elect, says: “I will confess to the Lord, and it will please him more than a young calf that grows horns and hooves. Let the poor see it and be glad.”
And again he says: “Sacrifice to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High. Call on me in the day of your trouble, and I will rescue you, and you will glorify me.”
For the sacrifice to God is a broken spirit.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening statement about God's lack of need, kept each quotation clearly attributed to David, and preserved the scriptural references and wording while making the sentences flow naturally for modern readers.
Clarified the opening contrast by making the one thing God requires explicit, and kept the scriptural quotations clearly attributed to David with their references intact.
Clarified that David is one of the elect, matching the work's terminology for God's chosen people, and kept the divine titles consistent.

notes.why: Key concept rendered inconsistently; reader may miss that all refer to the same group.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'the elect' or 'the elect of God' throughout.

notes.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
notes.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

fixed: The 'Master' vs 'Lord' issue is not a real problem: the source uses δεσπότης (Master) in the first sentence and κύριος (Lord) in the quotation, so the English correctly reflects the source's distinction.

last_rejected.ruling: ἀδελφοί literally 'brothers'; 'brothers and sisters' is standard inclusive rendering within normal range, not a major error.
